source_review.notes: Checked all ten final NASA, NIST, and FAA URLs on 2026-08-31; every URL returned HTTP 200. Reviewed current NASA Product Verification, Product Validation, Product Realization, Product Integration, V&V planning, and NPR process guidance; NIST source-context glossary entries; FAA lifecycle V&V guidance; and the NASA/SP-2016-6105 Rev. 2 handbook. Agency vocabulary is attributed and bounded rather than presented as universal certification or compliance policy.

evidence: Reviewed evidence tuple E=(O,R,C,M,P,D,Q,A,L) and definition of every component.
Reviewed configuration- and baseline-bounded verification and validation judgment notation.
Reviewed trace relations from requirements to evidence and expectations through scenarios to evidence.
Reviewed distinction among evaluation result, finding, disposition, authorization, and assurance claim.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation is an accountability structure, not a numerical proof or assertion that evidence is objective merely because it is recorded.

evidence: Executed verification-validation-distinction-fixture under python3 with exact output recorded in artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-071/report.json.
Confirmed four of four declared requirements verify in the synthetic result.
Confirmed two of three stakeholder expectations validate and the surge-prioritization expectation remains a gap.
Confirmed acceptance is explicitly not decided by either synthetic technical result.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Boolean synthetic counts demonstrate logical separation only; they omit evidence pedigree, coverage, uncertainty, criticality, configuration, and representativeness.

evidence: Confirmed verification pass does not imply validation pass by the omitted-need counterexample.
Confirmed validation evidence does not imply verification by the useful-prototype/nonconforming-audit counterexample.
Confirmed evidence cannot validly support a baseline or configuration it did not evaluate.
Confirmed a shared activity may support both purposes only through distinct references, oracles, traces, and conclusions.
Confirmed coverage ratios are diagnostics rather than sufficiency theorems.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The chapter derives claim boundaries and counterexamples but does not claim a formal completeness theorem for V&V.

evidence: Challenged well-formed but wrong requirements, useful but nonconforming prototypes, obsolete baselines, and configuration drift.
Reviewed nominal, boundary, overload, invalid input, race, partial/common-cause failure, degraded, maintenance, recovery, stale/corrupt data, observability-loss, and security cases.
Reviewed unrepresentative users, workload, data, environments, external services, test articles, and operational procedures.
Reviewed finite sampling, zero-failure claims, statistical assumptions, simulator/model validity, and independence limits.
Reviewed anomalies, test-error assertions, retests, waiver versus satisfaction, acceptance, certification, heritage/COTS reuse, and use drift.
Reviewed all ten worked examples and five complete answers for assumptions, reasoning, evidence limits, and bounded conclusions.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Real use requires domain, stakeholder, user/operator/maintainer, requirements, test, statistical, human-factors, model/simulation, safety/security, configuration, quality, regulatory, independent V&V, acceptance, and certification authority review as applicable.

evidence: Confirmed every claim names object/configuration and reference baseline.
Confirmed specified-requirement conformance remains distinct from stakeholder/intended-use fitness.
Confirmed requirements V&V, product verification, system validation, qualification, acceptance, and certification remain distinct.
Confirmed evidence binds environment, procedure, participants, tools/instrumentation, data, anomalies, and limitations.
Confirmed human, organizational, external-system, data, degraded-mode, and recovery context remain visible where relevant.
Confirmed change triggers impact analysis and selective re-verification/re-validation rather than automatic evidence reuse.
invariant_checking.notes: No test count, demonstration, user signature, simulator run, waiver, retest, heritage label, or production telemetry is presented as sufficient unbounded proof.

proof_review.notes: The chapter uses logical counterexamples and evidence structures but presents no theorem proof.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: The executable output is labeled synthetic_trace_and_scenario_results_only.
The fixture disclaims real verification, validation, readiness, safety, and acceptance conclusions.
Official guidance is attributed without claiming local compliance, certification, or approval.
Operational telemetry and observations are bounded by population, configuration, context, measurement, bias, and causal limits.
No external review, production V&V, acceptance, certification, or risk authorization is claimed.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Synthetic logic, source-backed process guidance, internal review, and operational assurance are explicitly separated.

conceptual_review.notes: Internal conceptual review checked verification, validation, object, reference, evidence, representativeness, oracle, qualification, acceptance, certification, anomaly, requirements V&V, product V&V, recursion, iteration, and evidence reuse.

practitioner_review.notes: Internal practitioner-oriented review checked planning and readiness, method selection, configuration/article pedigree, environment and human representativeness, end-to-end scenarios, statistical/model limits, independence, anomaly and waiver handling, acceptance/certification separation, operational monitoring, and change impact.

pedagogical_review.notes: Internal pedagogical review confirmed progression from the object-reference distinction through lifecycle mechanics, evidence boundaries, anomalies, governance, and operational drift. Ten distinct examples and five complete solutions cover requirements, physical systems, clinical software, simulation, services, suppliers, waivers, and adaptive systems.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external NASA/NIST/FAA expert, standards body, regulator, customer or stakeholder, user/operator/maintainer, requirements or test engineer, statistician, human-factors specialist, model/simulation authority, safety/security specialist, configuration or quality authority, independent V&V organization, acceptance authority, or certification body review is claimed.
